children: The Indonesian rupiah hovered around IDR 17,750 per U.S. dollar on Monday, steadying after recent weakness as House Commission XI approved Destry Damayanti as Bank Indonesia’s new governor for 2026–2031, succeeding Perry Warjiyo, who abruptly resigned in July.
Destry pledged that closer policy coordination with the government would not compromise BI’s independence, stressing stability and growth as priorities.
Meanwhile, the dollar held near a two-week high following hawkish remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, lifting expectations for a September rate hike.
Focus now shifts to key domestic data, including August inflation and July trade.
Inflation eased to 2.88% year-on-year, a three-month low and within BI’s 1-1/2%–3-1/2% target.
Meanwhile, June posted a second straight monthly trade deficit, driven by surging oil and gas imports, underscoring persistent external pressures.
For the month, the rupiah is on track to post the first gain in six months, up around 1.4% so far.

title: Rupiah Steady as Destry Confirmed as New BI Governor
